hints.text: The outside function $\ln u$ has derivative $\frac{1}{u} \cdot u'$. Here the inside is $u = \cos x$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\ln(x^2)$: its derivative is $\frac{1}{x^2} \cdot 2x = \frac{2}{x}$. The shape is the same here: one over the inside, times the derivative of the inside.
The chain rule gives $f'(x) = \frac{1}{\cos x} \cdot (-\sin x) = -\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = -\tan x$. Substitute $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$ and evaluate the tangent.
Since $\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1$, the value of the derivative is $f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1$.

explanation: By the chain rule, the derivative is one over the inside times the derivative of the inside: $\frac{d}{dx}\ln(\cos x) = \frac{1}{\cos x} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}\cos x$.
The derivative of the inside is $-\sin x$, so the result simplifies to $f'(x) = -\frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = -\tan x$.

At $x = \frac{\pi}{4}$, $\sin$ and $\cos$ are equal, so $\tan\frac{\pi}{4} = 1$ and $f'\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1$. The function is falling, since $\cos x$ shrinks toward $0$ as $x$ heads to $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Common trap
steps: Forgetting the inside gives $\frac{1}{\cos x}$, which at $\frac{\pi}{4}$ is $\sqrt{2} \approx 1.41$: positive, yet $\ln(\cos x)$ is clearly decreasing there.
Secant slope $\frac{-0.3512 - (-0.3412)}{0.01} \approx -1.0$. The chain-rule answer $-1$ is the one the numbers support.
